business_problem: Legacy on-prem analytics had outages, high maintenance, and weak predictive capability, making it hard for GLS to forecast deliveries accurately and provide reliable parcel-status insight.
solution_summary: GLS replaced its aging on-premises warehouse with Snowflake on AWS to make delivery analytics faster, cheaper, and more predictive. After refreshing the core parcel-system data model, Snowflake became both the central store for parcel data and the platform for a new data-mesh operating model. Instead of routing every report request through one central team, satellite teams can work directly with governed data while Snowflake absorbs heavy queries without disrupting operations. GLS also layered a natural-language AI interface on top so users can ask questions in plain language and have them translated into SQL and visualized results. Faster warehouse performance cut last-mile reports from 12 hours to one and monthly closing reports from a day to two hours, while near-zero maintenance removed operational drag. The result is earlier route planning, faster bottleneck detection, and more dependable delivery forecasts across 220 countries and territories.

solution_components.name: Snowflake

data_flow: Parcel and operations data is loaded into Snowflake on AWS, where data-mesh teams query governed datasets directly and natural-language requests are translated into SQL for self-service analysis. Resulting forecasts and operational reports feed route planning, depot operations, and customer delivery estimates.
business_outcome: GLS achieved 92% faster report generation, cut total operational expenditure 50%, eliminated disruption from heavy queries, and uses faster analytics to give customers more reliable delivery forecasts.
